label: The Levi-Civita Connection
notes: This chapter occupies printed pages 115 through 150 and singles out one connection from the infinitely many a manifold admits. We motivate why a metric alone should fix a canonical way to differentiate vector fields, previewing the two conditions and the uniqueness theorem that crown the chapter.

label: Connections, a Reminder
notes: A connection lets us differentiate one vector field along another while staying inside the tangent bundle. Recall its tensoriality in the first slot and Leibniz behaviour in the second, and note that without extra conditions there are infinitely many connections on a single smooth manifold.

label: Metric Compatibility
notes: Metric compatibility says the connection commutes with the inner product through a product rule. Equivalently parallel transport along any curve is a linear isometry, so transported frames stay orthonormal and angles and lengths are preserved exactly as the vectors are carried along.

label: Torsion and Symmetry
notes: The torsion tensor measures the failure of the connection to be symmetric in its two arguments. A symmetric, or torsion-free, connection satisfies the bracket identity, so mixed covariant derivatives differ only by the Lie bracket and second derivatives of functions stay symmetric.

label: The Fundamental Theorem
notes: The fundamental theorem of Riemannian geometry asserts that on every Riemannian or pseudo-Riemannian manifold there exists one and only one connection that is simultaneously metric compatible and torsion-free. This unique object is named the Levi-Civita connection and underlies all later curvature theory.

label: Existence and Uniqueness via Koszul
notes: The Koszul formula expresses the inner product of the covariant derivative entirely through the metric and Lie brackets. Because its right side never mentions the connection, it both forces uniqueness and constructs existence, since the right side defines a genuine connection satisfying both required conditions.

label: Christoffel Symbols
notes: In a coordinate chart the Koszul formula collapses to the classical Christoffel symbol formula built from first derivatives of the metric components and the inverse metric. These symbols are not tensors, yet they encode the connection completely and let us compute covariant derivatives explicitly.

label: The Tangential Connection
notes: For a submanifold of Euclidean space the tangential connection projects the ambient flat derivative back onto the tangent space. This projected operation is metric compatible and symmetric, so by uniqueness it must equal the intrinsic Levi-Civita connection of the induced metric.

label: Naturality under Isometries
notes: The Levi-Civita connection is determined by the metric alone, so any isometry carries one chapter's connection to another. Pushforward through an isometry intertwines the covariant derivatives, which is why every metric invariant we build from this connection is automatically an isometry invariant.

label: Worked Computation
notes: We assemble the Christoffel symbols of a simple diagonal metric to show the machinery in motion. Each nonzero symbol traces to a derivative of a metric coefficient, illustrating how curvature of coordinate lines is read directly from the connection without ever leaving the chart.

label: Common Pitfalls
notes: Students often forget that Christoffel symbols are not tensors and that torsion-freeness is a choice, not an automatic property. We stress that symmetry refers to the lower indices, that compatibility is about the metric, and that both are needed for the connection to be Levi-Civita.

label: Recap and Outlook
notes: We close by restating the two defining conditions, the uniqueness theorem, and the two formulas that compute the connection. The Levi-Civita connection now becomes the fixed platform on which geodesics, parallel transport, and the Riemann curvature tensor are built in the chapters ahead.
